behavior_notes: Filed from the PG-K audit; no implementation or terminal evidence is claimed by this row. The finding is measured, not inferred: workspace-wide there are zero [[bench]] targets, zero benches/ directories, zero criterion dependencies and zero files matching *baseline*, against a README sentence asserting that every one of fifteen gates has a bench binary, a committed baseline, a variance budget and a flame artifact.

PG-K RE-DERIVED at HEAD 90b472ea rather than inherited, because the orchestrator flagged the prior answer as unverified. The hypothesis was that PG-K gates bignum against a GMP-backed Reference while D1 forbids gmp-sys, so the ratio would have no measurable denominator. THAT IS FALSE. D1 governs what FrankenLean LINKS, not what it TIMES; the denominator is upstream's binary, whose GMP-backing is a property of upstream. Measured on this host: the pinned toolchain ships its own lib/libgmp.a and lib/lean/libleanshared.so exports 430 __gmp dynamic symbols, so the denominator is installed and real. Plan section 19.1 does not merely permit this, it COMMISSIONS it: W1 publishes a checked-in baseline report measuring the Reference at the pin. PG-K is therefore UNMEASURED, not unmeasurable. The reading also proves too much: nine of the fifteen gates are Reference-denominated and two name components D1 forbids us (GMP under PG-K, CaDiCaL under PG-9, whose binary sits in the same bin/ directory) - the ratio measuring what we gained by not having them is the point, not a contradiction.

REPAIR SHAPE: the README now states the plan's rule (a constraint on benchmark BUNDLES) instead of an inventory of containers, and discloses the measured cardinality inline in the PG-5 style. The join is mechanised in both directions - claim row PERF-GATE-BENCH-APPARATUS is Enforced so the overclaim cannot return, its citation requires the replacement disclosure to stay present, and the suite resolves the workspace members and fails if the disclosed count and the measured count disagree. Counting only [[bench]] sections would have been a false clean, since cargo auto-discovers a benches/ directory with no manifest section at all.

Records a defect shape absent from the AGENTS.md item 7 table: all six instances there are a claim whose evidence exists with the join to it unwatched. The bead's own evidence anchor needed re-anchoring: it recorded verification at HEAD 828d9488, which the 2026-07-25 filter-branch rewrite left unreachable from main (git merge-base --is-ancestor fails). Every count in this row was re-measured at 90b472ea rather than carried over - which is the same defect family the bead is about, one floor down: a verification claim and the commit it was made at.

The row records what tested SOUND as well, because most of the performance story is careful. The gate NUMBERS are correctly framed as TARGETED rather than OBSERVED; plan section 19.2 states the requirement in the correct modality (every benchmark BUNDLE records, a rule) and only the README restatement turns it into an inventory; fln-bignum documents its own schoolbook mul as deferred to PG-K rather than claiming performance; and fln-bench is a scrupulous 4281-line evidence substrate whose own doc says it does not run a product benchmark. THE GUARD DOES NOT EXEMPT ITS OWN FILE. Four of the 44 counted raw occurrences are inside tree_identity.rs and are counted rather than excluded, because a guard that excuses its own file cannot see a regression added to it (fln-8zsq's lesson). The census needles are assembled from fragments so the scanner's own literals stay out of the population it measures, and a planted-site test proves the assembled needles still match the real spellings - an escaped needle that matched nothing would turn every count into a confident zero.

STAGE 1'S DIMENSIONS WERE DECIDED, NOT CODED, which is what item 3 of the bead asked for. dt5's criteria name name-depth and canonical-byte limits. Name depth is real and unbounded -- fln-core's Name::append_core records that a name's component chain is unbounded and attacker-reachable. Canonical bytes are the WRONG quantity: the merge pipeline never encodes a descriptor, so a limit on bytes stage 1 does not emit would be joined to a producer nothing makes it consult. What stage 1 spends is component bytes, and that is what is bounded; the_descriptor_byte_dimension_is_not_the_canonical_encoding_length measures that the two numbers differ so the distinction cannot quietly become false.

STRUCTURE WHERE IT WAS AVAILABLE. Item 4's 'exhausted case leaves inputs, roots and sharing unchanged' is not tested as control flow: merge takes three shared references and can obtain nothing else, so no path through it can move them. behavior_notes: A STALE CLAIM FIXED IN PASSING, and it is the same defect class one level down. Shape::WITNESS named DefEqBinder and described it as the deepest-per-level descent, i.e. the one that overflows first. The measurement contradicts that: defeq binder congruence uses two kernel frames per level and is nonetheless the CHEAPEST of the four, so it overflows LAST. The witness still fired, because Budget::DEFAULT on 2 MiB overflows on any shape -- which is exactly why nobody noticed. A witness that passes for a reason other than the one stated beside it is evidence that has stopped being true without anything going red. WITNESS is now the measured worst.

COST: twelve subprocess probes, no bisection, 0.18 seconds for the whole file including the four pre-existing guards. The stack is 4 MiB on purpose -- the prediction substitutes STACK_ENTRY_RESERVE_BYTES for the measured intercept, an error under 1% at that size and 4% at 1 MiB, which at 1 MiB would eat into the band.

IT BRACKETS RATHER THAN RE-DERIVES. The check never recomputes the constant and compares the result to itself, which would be the same number twice and would prove nothing. It asks the real descent questions whose answers are only all correct when the claim is true, and it takes the claim as a PARAMETER so the planted violations can hand it deliberately wrong numbers -- half the true cost, three times the true cost, and an entry reserve of 8 KiB -- and require a refusal naming the specific direction. A check that cannot fail is a rubber stamp.

THE DRIFT IS MEASURED, NOT HYPOTHESISED. Two observations on 2026-07-25, both on franken_lean-kxbj's row: the same instrument read 5,935.3 bytes/depth on the development host and 6,553.6 on an RCH remote worker at the identical (profile, arch, os); and widening Budget for franken_lean-4o3n cost two of the four shapes one level of ceiling. Neither was caught by anything. Both were caught because a human re-ran an ignored test on a hunch.

THE GUARDS THAT ALREADY EXISTED PROVE SURVIVAL AT THE SHIPPED PAIRING, which is a different claim from the shipped number still describing the descent. With STACK_SAFETY_FACTOR at 2 and MIN_STACK_BYTES rounded up on top of it there is roughly 3x of headroom in which MEASURED_STACK_BYTES_PER_DEPTH can be fiction and every test still passes -- and when the headroom finally runs out the guard does not fail, it aborts the test binary uncatchably. The tripwire turns the safety factor from a silent absorber of drift into a margin with a tripwire in it.

THE TOLERANCES ARE JUSTIFIED RATHER THAN PICKED. High 25%: that is 2.4x the largest host-to-host spread yet observed (10.4%), so ordinary machine variation cannot redden the tree, and it is half of STACK_SAFETY_FACTOR, so it fires with the whole margin still unspent. Low 33%, deliberately looser, because the directions differ in consequence -- an understated constant is the direction that aborts processes, while an overstated one is not a safety failure but silently shrinks depth_for_stack_bytes for every caller and manufactures typed non-answers that nobody can tell from real ones, which under franken_lean-4o3n is exactly what erodes a consensus seat.

THE TWO DIRECTIONS ARE QUANTIFIED DIFFERENTLY, and getting that wrong would have made this a flake generator rather than a guard. ABOVE the claim is a property of ANY shape -- one descent costing more than the constant says is enough to make MIN_STACK_BYTES promise too little. BELOW the claim is a property of ALL shapes at once, because the constant is the MAXIMUM over the four descents and a single cheap descent is not evidence that it is overstated. defeq_binder measures 4,507 bytes/depth against the shipped 5,935, which is 24% below it BY DESIGN; a per-shape low bound would have parked a permanent tripwire 9 points from a correct value, and the first person to see it fire would have widened the band rather than read it. Caught while reading the numbers back, before landing.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER: it re-checks the constant on the machine and profile the suite happens to run in, which is the configuration that matters (cargo test) and is not every configuration. It is a benchmark-class bound (D7) with a stated margin, not a theorem, and it does not make ExecConfig able to distinguish two hosts that share a triple -- franken_lean-4o3n's row argues against narrowing it, because that would make every budget Extrapolated the moment it crossed a machine.

behavior_notes: BOTH JOINS ARE NOW CLOSED, which is what this bead closes on. List->marker fails four ways (a name neither marked nor declared not-yet-seeded; a not-yet-seeded declaration whose crate has stopped being a stub; a declaration that outlived its own repair; and an empty scan, refused as broken rather than read as clean). Marker->kill is a campaign that plants each seedable mutant and requires the NAMED killers to die FOR THE STATED REASON, retained by a per-commit receipt keyed by a digest over the mutated site and the killer bodies, so gutting a marked test expires the recorded kill mechanically.

DYING IS NOT ENOUGH; DYING FOR THE RIGHT REASON IS THE CLAIM. Measured live: with the positivity check skipped, the bad block is still REJECTED -- for "block declares 0 recursors" -- so a rig accepting any non-zero exit would have scored that mutant killed by a test that had stopped testing positivity at all.

MEASURED, NOT INHERITED, at 115ef2fd on this host: 3 of 3 seedable mutants planted and killed in 12,102 ms, production files confirmed restored. The two absent names (leaked transaction assignment, stale cache hit accepted) target fln-elab and fln-ledger, which are charter-only stubs; no_plant_exists_for_a_name_that_cannot_be_seeded_yet refuses a recipe for either, so a plant against a stub cannot become theatre, and the reminder fires the moment either crate stops being a stub.

THE CADENCE HALF: a dispatcher exists (.github/workflows/mandated-mutants.yml, weekly cron plus workflow_dispatch) and the receipt's class token is DERIVED from what actually dispatches the campaign by one function shared with the writer, so the two cannot drift. Five mutants killed it in both directions; the sharpest is dropping --ignored, because the campaign is #[ignore]d and a libtest filter matching nothing exits 0 -- a lane green forever while running no campaign.

THE EXCLUSION IS UNIFORM RATHER THAN SELF-REFERENTIAL (the franken_lean-2ki4 correction): every scanned file is cut at its first source-reading construct, this one included, because a file that reads source at test time is a guard from that point on.

THE GUARD'S OWN FIRST VERSION FAILED ITS OWN MUTATION CAMPAIGN and the survivor is recorded because it is the finding inside the finding. Deleting the exclusion entirely SURVIVED: the self-check asserted this file yields no markers, which was true whether or not the exclusion worked, because the marker constant escapes its inner quote and never matched the runtime needle. A check passing for a reason unrelated to its property is fln-8zsq's defect reproduced inside the guard written to prevent it. Repaired with an unescaped decoy marker below the cut.

THE SECTION 18 NAMES ARE DERIVED FROM AGENTS.md AT TEST TIME, never transcribed (the franken_lean-869w lesson, where ten of ten hand-copied G0 questions were wrong). A short or failed parse refuses rather than enforcing a truncated list as if it were complete.

WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM, and it is filed as fln-s8oo rather than left implicit: that a dispatched run ever OCCURRED. The token attests a CONFIGURED cadence, never a kept one -- GitHub disables scheduled workflows after inactivity and nothing inside the tree can tell that from a cron that fired. Separately, the dispatch reader is a text scan, so it attests a workflow is DECLARED, not LOADABLE. Each campaign run remains one measurement at one commit on one host, class bounded_model; what runs per commit is the retention and cadence checks, not the campaign.

COST: about 25 s for the one-time -Zbuild-std compile, then under 3 s for all four lanes warm -- four times cheaper than the Miri set, because TSAN instruments native code instead of interpreting it. Neither detector subsumes the other: Miri finds UB with no observable effect on this hardware (which is the class the fixed defect belonged to, since aligned 32-bit loads do not tear) and TSAN runs real threads, the real allocator, and the syscalls Miri refuses.

EVIDENCE-ARRAY CORRECTION, cc_2: the first version of this row carried eight behavior notes and EMPTY unit/boundary/error/mutation arrays, and I reported it as carrying real evidence. It did not — it was narrative with no citations, which is the defect class this manifest exists to prevent, in my own row. The citations are now present, and the hand-run ones say so in their own text so nobody reads them as a standing lane.

IT FAILS ON THE REAL DEFECT. With dec_ref's mode probe reverted to the plain ptr::read it had before 8cd1d3b, against the real crate on the pinned toolchain, TSAN reports two data races -- core::ptr::read::<i32> and core::sync::atomic::atomic_sub::<i32,i32> -- and the process exits 66. Restored, exit 0. The revert was made by hand, run, and reverted; git confirms crates/fln-unsafe-abi clean afterwards, and nothing of it is committed.

OPERATIONAL TRAP FOUND WHILE MEASURING, and it decides whether a lane is real: on the planted defect libtest prints 'test result: ok. 1 passed' and the process THEN exits 66, because TSAN reports at teardown. A lane that greps for 'test result: ok', or reads the last line, reports a clean run while a data race was detected and printed. The exit code is the only reliable signal. This is recorded in the guard document because a wiring that gets it wrong is a green rubber stamp.

PARTIAL: this row covers the DETECTOR half only. The CI lane that runs these commands is .github/workflows/ci.yml and scripts/check.sh, both cod_2's surface, and is handed over on the bead rather than claimed here. The bead stays in progress.

THE RUNNABLE LANE NOW EXISTS AS A SCRIPT; what remains is only its registration, which is cod_2 surface (.github/workflows/ci.yml and scripts/check.sh). The hard half -- getting TSAN to build at the pin, the exit-code semantics, the isolated target directory, and proving each lane actually ran -- is done and measured. Registration is two lines.

THE TWO DETECTORS NAME THE SAME RACE FROM OPPOSITE ENDS -- Miri says non-atomic read versus atomic read-modify-write and points at rc.rs; TSAN points at the core primitives each side bottoms out in. That agreement is worth something precisely because neither was derived from the other, which is the same argument as B3's two engines one layer down.

TSAN IS REACHABLE AT THE PIN, and the earlier claim that it was not was wrong for the same reason the earlier claim about Miri was wrong: nobody had installed rust-src for the pinned nightly and tried. -Zbuild-std rebuilds std under the same -Zsanitizer=thread, which removes the ABI-mismatch refusal that made it look impossible. Verified instrumented rather than assumed: 444 __tsan symbols in the test binary, including __tsan_func_entry and __tsan_atomic, and libstd rebuilt under the same flags.

The executed-check discriminates, observed rather than asserted: its first version compared the cargo FILTER against the printed test name, and `concurrent_publication` is a prefix of `concurrent_publication_of_one_target_never_yields_a_mixture`, so a lane that ran correctly was reported ran=no. Fixed to require the exact name, and the episode is recorded in the script because a guard that cannot tell "did not run" from "I do not recognise that name" is one that gets widened the first time it fires.

The guard reports THREE outcomes, not two: 0 pass, 1 a detector finding or a lane that did not run, 2 setup could not be established. Separated because "we could not look" is not "we looked and found nothing" (FL-INV-07), and a missing component must not read as a clean run.

The lanes must use an isolated CARGO_TARGET_DIR: -Zsanitizer=thread invalidates every artifact built without it, so sharing the workspace target directory would force a full rebuild for the next pane and another when they rebuild without it.

rust-toolchain.toml now declares miri and rust-src as components of the existing pin. SUITE.lock governs the CHANNEL, which is unchanged, so this is not a second pin; it is what makes a fresh clone able to run either guard at all.

behavior_notes: CLOSED ON A CORRECTED SCOPE, NOT ON THE ORIGINAL. This bead asked for 'serialization preserving sharing exactly in BOTH codecs'. The two codecs want OPPOSITE properties and only one of them is even coherent. fln-hash's Canonical is documented as 'a value with exactly one canonical encoding under a frozen schema', so a sharing-SENSITIVE encoder there would give one value many encodings depending on construction history and would move every content-addressed digest resting on it. Sharing preservation is a DEFECT in that codec, not a feature. What is pinned instead is its dual: sharing-independence.

THAT SECOND ERROR IS THE FAMILY IN AGENTS.md ITEM 8, ONE FLOOR UP: do not assert against a downstream value that a later stage repairs. hv9m was the same shape at the digest level, which is why its test had to be written against the encoder. Here the repairing stage is the interner. It is the first recorded instance where the unguarded thing is an ACCEPTANCE CRITERION rather than a digest, a key, a lint or a lane.

THE DISCRIMINATOR FOR THE WRITE HALF, so it is not re-derived when the encoder exists: encoded BYTE LENGTH, or decode-observed node count, against the INTERNED node count. Not store size after a re-intern, for the reason above.

THE OLEAN READ HALF IS PINNED ON A REAL PINNED-REFERENCE ARTIFACT (tribunal/fixtures/c3/Init.SizeOfLemmas.olean), not a constructed buffer. DeclDecoder::decode_expr memoises on the object offset, so two slots pointing at one object become two references to one Expr node. The test counts tree POSITIONS against DISTINCT node pointers and requires a DAG. Pointer identity is the only discriminator: structural equality cannot see it (a tree and a DAG denoting one term are ==) and neither can a round trip, which a sharing-losing decoder also passes.

THE WRITE HALF IS RE-HOMED, NOT DROPPED. fln-olean is decode-only: decode_expr at crates/fln-olean/src/decl.rs:537 has no encoder beside it and `rg 'fn encode|fn write_'` over that file returns nothing. Writing one is codec-sized work and belongs to franken_lean-0nz (W2 olean codec write, byte-identical faithful emission), with franken_lean-0vf (G0-5 re-emit spike) the place to price sharing as one of the serialization freedoms it exists to enumerate. Closing this bead does not retire that requirement; it moves it to the bead that owns the encoder.

TWO PREMISES IN THE BEAD'S OWN TEXT WERE FALSE AND I WROTE THEM. (a) 'There is NO Expr writer anywhere in the workspace... CanonWriter is a HASHING encoder with no inverse' - false: canon.rs:1044 implements Canonical for Expr with write_body AND read_body, and expr_round_trip_property already exercises the round trip. (b) The prescribed check - 're-intern the result and assert the STORE SIZE is the same' - CANNOT DETECT the defect it was written for: re-interning restores sharing, so store sizes match on both sides while the wire form lost all of it. The check is green against the defect.

On any target other than x86_64-linux the shipped measurement is Grade::Extrapolated, so no cross-engine comparison can be established there at all. A platform-matrix run would report zero disagreements, and zero disagreements would be the wrong thing to conclude.

Parity here is parity of the DERIVATION, never of the number. A bound detached from the configuration it was measured in is a number; attached to it, it is a measurement. Every claim in this row rests on the second, and on nothing the first would support.

THIS DOES NOT EARN AGREEMENT BETWEEN TWO ENGINES. There is no second engine: no NbE anywhere in the workspace, and fln-checker is an independence boundary and a data schema, not an implementation that decides verdicts. Fuel parity today is a property of ONE engine against its own execution configuration. A reader who takes 'fuel parity, tested' to mean the engines have been compared would be wrong, and that is the sentence most likely to be dropped when this row is summarised.

The measured dev/release gap is the evidence, not an illustration: 5,935 bytes of native stack per unit of depth in dev against 640 in release, for the identical depth 4096, same code and same target (bead franken_lean-kxbj). That is why an agreed depth NUMBER certifies nothing.

THE LAW IS SATISFIABLE FOR ALL 42, which is why this is worth fixing rather than tolerating: a comment added today to a bead closed last week has created_at > closed_at, and 36 of the 42 already carry at least one comment. THE FIX AND ITS DIRECTION, recorded so it is not re-derived. Bind the DISCLOSED exempt population to the MEASURED one, equality in BOTH directions, plus the conservation identity exempt + bound == complete as the anti-vacuity guard so a predicate that stops classifying fails loudly instead of reporting a clean zero. Equality both ways is correct here and one-way-plus-floor is not: that shape is for a declared remainder of permitted violations, which shrinks as people repair it, whereas this is a disclosure of a measured population that does not move under repair at all -- repairing an exempt row does not change its bead's closed_at. It moves only when a row is added or removed for a pre-boundary bead, or a bead is reopened and re-closed, and every one of those should be seen. It is the bkw6 move: when the far end cannot be compared row by row, bind the claim to the cardinality of what it asserts.

WHAT WAS WRONG was that correctness rested on an accident nothing pinned, inside a function whose whole subject is identity. Level's own doc says its Debug is byte-identical to the derived rendering, so a field added or reordered in Level or its Node silently moves every digest preimage while every test stays green - the digest is a bucket hint confirmed by full Expr equality. The rendering also included Level's packed data word, a CACHED hash seed and depth, so the identity preimage depended on a cache rather than on structure.

behavior_notes: A LIMIT OF THE CONFIGURATION MODEL, found by re-measuring on two machines: the same instrument at the same (profile, arch, os) measured 5,935 bytes/depth on this host and 6,553.6 on an RCH remote worker, a 10.4% spread that ExecConfig cannot distinguish. Grade::Measured is therefore a claim about a configuration CLASS, not about a host. It is safe -- 6,553.6 x 4096 = 26.8 MiB actual against 46.4 MiB budgeted -- and this is the first time the 2x safety factor has been asked to do anything. Narrowing ExecConfig to a host identity would make every budget Extrapolated the moment it crossed a machine, which is worse than the margin it would buy.

A depth ceiling above the stack it runs on is not a bound, it is a bound-shaped comment. A native stack overflow aborts the process uncatchably, so FL-INV-07 cannot be satisfied after the fact by catching anything; the guarantee is structural or it does not exist. It is now structural: the ceiling-below-floor relation is a const assertion checked when the kernel compiles, not a test that has to be remembered.

CORPUS RERUN, the last acceptance clause, discharged at HEAD against the pinned Reference: all 2,433 modules, zero stack overflows, terminal summary reached, and Init.GrindInstances.Ring.SInt at index 412 is byte-identical to cod_3's pre-existing v8 census INCLUDING its stream_digest -- decoded=65, compared=61, disagreements=0, unscorable=4, subject_no_answer=4, with typed Depth for instCommRingInt16/Int64/Int32 and Steps for Int8. The worker stack is now Budget::MIN_STACK_BYTES, the kernel's own derived requirement, rather than a number picked to make a crash stop, so the clause about not using an unmeasured workaround is met in substance and not only in outcome.

RE-MEASURED at HEAD after franken_lean-4o3n widened Budget from 16 bytes to about 144: the slope is unchanged at 5,935.3 against a shipped 5,935. What moved is small and is recorded rather than fixed -- forall_infer and lam_infer each lost ONE level at both probe stacks while app_infer kept its, and the fitted intercept for those two rose by exactly one slope quantum, which is the coarsest unit a whole-depth bisection can report. So the true growth in fixed entry cost is in (0, 5935] bytes and this instrument cannot resolve it further. Cost: one unit of ceiling in 4,096, 0.02%, against a 64 KiB entry reserve that remains 2.4x the largest measured intercept.

THE LANE STILL EXITS 101, and not for this bead. It panics on fln-lst4's coverage clause -- kernel differential coverage silently stopped: 156972 < 157183 scoreable declarations -- with numbers identical to cod_3's v8, so nothing here regressed it and nothing here fixes it. That clause is cod_3's lane. A red lane exit is not evidence against this bead and is not claimed as evidence for it.

The number is measured, not chosen: 5,935 bytes of native stack per unit of depth, dev profile, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, taken black-box by bisecting the deepest surviving descent at two known stack sizes in a subprocess so the fixed entry cost solves out of the slope. depth stays 4,096 deliberately -- that is a POLICY choice about checking power, and the thing that was uncalibrated was the stack it silently assumed, so relocating 4,096 would have moved an uncalibrated bound rather than calibrating one.

The witness asserts the FAILURE as well as the fix: Budget::DEFAULT on a 2 MiB thread -- the exact pairing that killed the Tribunal on this module -- must STILL abort inside a contained subprocess, and the same run under Budget::for_stack_bytes(2 MiB) must not. If that test ever stops dying, the hazard has moved and the calibration is measuring the wrong thing. A silently-passing calibration is worse than no calibration.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER: a benchmark-class claim (D7) over four SYNTHETIC descents on one target at one optimisation level. It is not a proof that no corpus term is worse than forall_infer, and the 2x factor is a margin rather than a theorem. The strongest available follow-up is to run the real Init.GrindInstances.Ring.SInt declarations through the same probe at varying stack sizes and confirm they sit under the synthetic worst; that needs the olean decode path and belongs to the conformance lane.
